verdict.rationale: Luma's API exposes a wide range of generation features that also appear in the creative product: image and video generation, Multi-Keyframe sequence control, and native HDR/EXR export. It also ships two endpoints with Python/JS/TS SDKs. However, no documentation claims or demonstrates that everything in the UI is available through the API. The browser workspace, Luma Agents workflows, Skills, Modify Video V2, Reframe, motion and lighting transfer are described for the product but not shown to be API-reachable. missing for 10: explicit UI/API parity statement or feature matrix, API coverage of Skills/Agents workspace workflows and Ray editing features (Modify, Reframe, motion/lighting transfer), independent hands-on confirmation of parity.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can do everything through the API that I can do in the UI

citations.quote: Dream Machine API let's developers use image and video generation capabilities.
Two endpoints, Python/JS/TS SDKs, credit-based pricing, production-grade from day one
Sequence-level control, exposed at the API.
Native HDR Generation and 16-bit EXR Export so AI work composites alongside live-action plates in your users' Resolve or Nuke.
